access/cedar-examples/documentCloud#the.note: Suspected real bug (in an example policy set). The README says owners delete their documents ("DeleteDocument: Only the owner should be able do this"), but policies.cedar has no permit for DeleteDocument at all (the README's own snippet names Action::"deleteDocument", which is not in the schema). The Cedar engine (cedar-wasm 4.14.0) denies alice deleting her own unblocked document, authenticated, with no determining policy. A decision: its counterexample is a witness request, not a run, so score.ts reports it as unknown.

Suspected real bug (in an example; the intent is the README's, which is ambiguous). The README calls Public "a principal that represents an un-authenticated user" that "can view only when explicitly permitted", but the forbid at policies.cedar:108-109 denies every request whose context has is_authenticated false, Public::"public" included: Cedar denies the unauthenticated public view of alice_public (publicAccess "view", not private) by policy13 and allows it only when the request claims is_authenticated true. Also, entities.json names the Public entity Public::"unauthenticated" while the policies name Public::"public". A decision: score.ts reports it as unknown (witness, no run).

access/kubernetes/rbacRuleAllows#a rule.note: Refuted with a rule whose ResourceNames lists "": the original RuleAllows (v1.37.1) allows `create pods` (no name) by ResourceNames [""] and denies it by ["web"]. The whitelist matches the empty name like any other; the docs' claim (resourceNames cannot restrict create) is about rules that name real resources. Restated as "a rule naming only non-empty resources never allows an unnamed request".
The restatement of "a rule naming resources never allows an unnamed request" (refuted by ResourceNames [""], confirmed on the original); proven.
